title: IR mode and WebAssembly: one source, two targets (and where SPIR-V stands)
summary: Drake's omc has an IR mode: a first line ir makes it write OSC IR v1 for scalar functions. A back end written in Omega, seed/wasm/irwasm.om, turns that IR into an import-free WebAssembly module. I'll show you the same functions running natively and in wasm with the same answers, traps included. SPIR-V is an open pull request (#804), not on the pinned commit, so for now it is PROPOSED.
goal: Compile scalar Omega functions to AArch64 and to WebAssembly through IR mode and irwasm, and state the SPIR-V status honestly.
key_steps: Keep the IR unit to scalar functions calling earlier functions
Prepend an ir line and compile: { printf "ir\n"; cat fns.om; } | omc > fns.ir
Compile seed/wasm/irwasm.om with omc and run it on the IR to get fns.wasm
Load and call the module with a wasm engine (Node here, read-only)
Compare against the native build, traps included

example.code:
note fns.om: plain scalar functions. One source, two targets: AArch64 and WebAssembly
fn gcd a uint b uint to uint
while ne b 0 bound 64
t = rem a b
a = b
b = t
end
ret a
end
fn lcm a uint b uint to uint
ret mul div a gcd a b b
end
fn tri n uint to uint
note 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1)
s = uint 0
for i uint n
s = add s i
end
ret s
end
fn addi a int b int to int
note signed add: overflow traps, it never wraps
ret add a b
end

common_mistake: Putting globals, text, arrays or host words in an IR unit (error 9 or 3), or reading a wasm RuntimeError as a specific Omega trap code (wasm does not keep it). Keep IR units scalar and compare with a native run when the code matters. And do not call SPIR-V supported until PR #804 merges and its gate runs.
evidence_note: Native and wasm runs recorded on Linux AArch64 with omc befb8199...8a1d and Node v24.21.0 as read-only oracle; byte-for-byte reproducible. Browser integration not exercised here. SPIR-V: PROPOSED (open PR #804, not at the pin, not run; spirv-val not installed). No GPU execution claimed.
